answer: Agents register a one‑time seed hashed on the ledger, then at a random block commit a lotus‑derived nonce and later reveal its preimage, proving ownership without early exposure. The network only accepts answers whose reveal matches the commitment and whose nonce contains the oasis keyword, so a Sybil attacker must generate a fresh commitment for every fake identity each round. Thus the attacker pays the full cost of solving a new hash puzzle and posting stake for each bogus node, driving the expense to the nadir of practicality.
